frequency_question: How often does a federal department execute a full accreditation revocation within 28 months of initial public dispute/signaling?
membership_rule: Includes any formal federal agency proceeding to strip an established national/professional accreditor of its recognition status. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probationary sanctions that do not result in ultimate loss of recognition.

cases.name: ABA accreditation standards challenges and reviews historically

provenance_note: 2 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 4 major federal challenges to established institutional/professional accreditors since 1980, with 1 resulting in complete termination of recognition.
known_gaps: Few exact historical precedents exist for professional association law school accreditors specifically, requiring generalization to all federally recognized accreditors.
skeleton: Federal oversight reviews of major accreditors per decade (approx 4 major challenges per decade over 40 years) multiplied by the historical proportion resulting in terminal revocation (1 out of 4 major contested challenges).
multiplier: 4 decades * 1 major challenge per decade = 4 total cases; 1 terminal revocation resulting in total loss of status.
validity_reason: Administrative law and Department of Education recognition procedures remain stable across multi-year regulatory cycles.
